family.description: The nature of the data. 'mdm': a master record of the organization, shared between modules — always the family of a role. 'tdm': the movement, the event, the operation of this module — the family of almost every table. 'ddm': what is recalculated from the others (a metric, a summary, a series) and has no writer, no lifecycle and no unique key.

storageKind.description: Where the rows live. 'platform' on every role, because the rows are the platform's. 'relational' on a table of the module, which is the usual answer. 'timeSeries' only when the rows are a series chunked by time, read by period and never updated. 'external' only on an external entity: the rows live in the connection, and the word is the neutral value of that family.

connectionId.description: A connection of the platform catalog, or a system a sibling module declares (both listed in the plan prompt), or, if neither serves, the name (lowerCamel, new) of a system this module declares in integration. Only on kind external. source is derived from it and is never sent.

retentionDays.description: Days a row of this table is kept after it is written, then erased. Only on a `timeSeries` table, and only when the request says so; absent = kept forever.
